title: Settled force initiation
effort: Produce a decisive knee, hip and ankle push from organized positions; express it upward and forward.
quality_marker: Within E1 record valid still-start takeoffs out of six attempts: no second dip, clear upward push, both feet receive together and the 2 s landing hold is controlled. Record arm position, depth, surface and any measured output only with a verified method. Use the listed attempts only; a miss or invalid attempt consumes the dose. Record actual attempts, setup and any substitutions; no bonus tests or comparison across unlike tasks.
brief: The still-start squat jump is the main task. Separate hip-driven implement motion, grounded ankle finish, forward projection, one-lead-leg rise and a small leg-driven release. Six direct strength jobs supply knee/hip extension, lead-leg contribution, knee-flexor leverage and both knee-angle plantar-flexion demands.

explosive.name: Squat Jump — settled quarter-squat start
explosive.job: Main knee/hip force from a still start, expressed vertically.
explosive.cue: Hold a comfortable quarter squat 2 s with hands at hips; jump vertically without another dip, land on both feet with yielding knees and hold 2 s. Keep jump height within a controlled reception.
explosive.replacement: a smaller same-start jump; if flight cannot be controlled, a fast nonflight squat rise at the same dose and zero landings
explosive.identity: squat-jump; plyometrics-all-cards.json; arm-fixed still-start execution declared
explosive.novelty_reason: Initial reference. A countermovement jump was considered, but the still start isolates force initiation before preload is emphasized.
explosive.rest_text: 90 s between complete set rounds; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Kettlebell Swing — dead-stop two-hand repetitions
explosive.job: Rapid hip extension moves a retained implement without adding landings.
explosive.cue: Hike a light kettlebell from a stable parked start, snap hips to a tall finish with a chest-level float, guide the return and park fully after each rep. No squat pull, arm lift or lumbar arch.
explosive.replacement: a very light rapid dumbbell hip hinge with a 2 s lowering and still finish if swing skill or grip is unconfirmed
explosive.identity: kettlebell-swing parent; migration 472 labels dead-stop as proposed new variant
explosive.novelty_reason: Initial hip-inertia task. A continuous swing would obscure the separate starts; park every repetition.
explosive.rest_text: 90 s between complete set rounds; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Calf Raise — rapid supported rise, no flight
explosive.key: Calf Raise — rapid supported rise, no flight
explosive.job: Express a quick ankle finish while keeping forefeet continuously grounded.
explosive.cue: With stable hand support and soft-straight knees, rise onto forefeet quickly, hold 1 s, lower 2 s to floor. No jump or bouncing heel drop.
explosive.replacement: a smaller unloaded quick heel rise with the same grounded dose
explosive.identity: standing-dumbbell-calf-raise parent; nonflight rapid bodyweight execution proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: Initial grounded ankle task. Pogos were deferred to avoid making every force task a landing drill.
explosive.rest_text: 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Standing Broad Jump — dip, project and stick
explosive.key: Standing Broad Jump — dip, project and stick
explosive.job: Direct a coordinated leg push forward, distinct from the vertical still-start task.
explosive.cue: One controlled dip and arm swing; jump forward from both feet and land on both feet, hold 2 s. Keep start and landing within the marked first 3 m and remaining 7 m clear.
explosive.replacement: a shorter two-foot projection, or a rapid nonflight squat rise if reception cannot stay organized; record removed landings
explosive.novelty_reason: Initial forward vector task. A second vertical variation would add less distinct directional practice.
explosive.rest_text: 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Step-Up — fast grounded drive, rear foot joins
explosive.key: Step-Up — fast grounded drive, rear foot joins
explosive.job: Let one lead leg supply upward force against a stable support without hand-off to a jump.
explosive.cue: Use a low inspected immovable step. Front whole foot planted; rise quickly without springing from the trailing foot, bring that foot onto the step, then descend under control in 3 s. No flight.
explosive.replacement: a supported fast split-squat rise with both feet grounded and the same per-leg dose if support fit fails
explosive.identity: bodyweight-step-up parent; nonflight rapid delivery proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: Initial independent lead-leg force task. A step-up jump was rejected because its additional receiving problem is unnecessary here.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 45 s, then the other leg; 4 total reps; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Medicine Ball Scoop Toss — hip-driven forward release
explosive.key: Medicine Ball Scoop Toss — hip-driven forward release
explosive.job: Transfer leg/hip extension into a freely released implement rather than a retained swing.
explosive.cue: Light ball between thighs, soft knees and hinge; drive hips tall and project forward/upward with long arms. Feet stay down, no trunk turn or catching return. Let the ball stop before retrieval.
explosive.replacement: three rapid light-dumbbell quarter-squat rises with heels grounded, 10 s between reps and the same next-section recovery; keep arms fixed and drive the load with the legs; log zero throws
explosive.identity: medicine-ball-scoop-toss; plyometrics-all-cards.json; forward nonflight execution declared
explosive.novelty_reason: Initial leg-driven release. Unlike E2, force ends in free projection; three throws keep the shared hinge demand modest.
explosive.rest_text: 20 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

resilience.name: Tibialis Raise — wall-supported
resilience.job: Light ankle dorsiflexor loading to control foot position before a stable push/landing.
resilience.cue: Back against an inspected wall, heels on floor; lift forefeet 2 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Adjust foot distance to stay easy.
resilience.replacement: a seated unweighted toe raise through comfortable range
resilience.identity: Verified family: tibialis-raise; wall-supported execution declared

resilience.name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction — light
resilience.job: Light lateral-hip strengthening to keep the pelvis and knee organized over the force-producing leg.
resilience.cue: Lie on side, lower leg bent; lift upper leg slightly 2 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s with toes facing forward and pelvis still. Bodyweight is sufficient unless clearly easy.
resilience.replacement: a smaller unloaded leg lift with the same per-leg dose
resilience.identity: Proposed exact execution; no verified canonical ID
resilience.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 30 s, then the other leg; 10 total reps; 60 s before the next exercise/section

primary.name: Hamstring Walkout — complete out-and-back cycle
primary.job: Knee-flexor leverage while the pelvis stays raised, distinct from moving through a hip hinge.
primary.cue: Start in a bilateral bridge. Each cycle is two small heel steps out per foot, then two back per foot: eight placements in about 8 s. Keep a soft knee and level hips; never chase a fully straight leg.
primary.replacement: a shorter-lever walkout at the same complete-cycle count; reduce range for sagging or cramp and stop if control does not return

E: Use light resistance or bodyweight that permits visibly rapid force with control. Begin with E1 while fresh. Each row has a distinct job; supporting work stays small. Rest may be extended to 2–3 minutes when speed, control or attention has not returned. Stop for pain, loss of alignment, stiff/asymmetric landing or clear slowing; rest and regress remaining work only if control returns, otherwise record stopped work. Never make up failed attempts. No drop landings or rotational throws are prescribed.
S: Light controlled strengthening, at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Do not chase burn, shaking or pre-fatigue. Reduce load/range when control fades; stop for symptoms.
P: Working sets are challenging at about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve. Select load/lever from demonstrated ability, not age or calendar week. Keep the stated controlled lowering and complete range; no forced repetitions, maximum testing or conditioning circuit. Check late-set and late-session quality; record reductions instead of forcing nominal completion.

setup: Use one inspected takeoff lane, one low step and stable hand support; no jumping down. Kettlebell and throw tasks require separate clearance and coach attention. If the minimum bell or ball cannot move quickly with control, use the listed same-slot version. Inspect stable supports, minimum loads, surface grip and all active/waiting/return paths. Keep one athlete active per lane under suitable supervision; no group size or station count is assumed. Three separate 10 m lanes are not a 30 m runway. Ball releases need separately verified flight/bounce/roll containment. Replacements occupy the original slot; missing readiness or equipment can change the practice exposure and actual totals. Before applying multiple replacements, check the other rows: a replacement must not duplicate an exercise already delivered in another slot. Do not add duplicate work just to fill the count. If the supplied replacements cannot preserve distinct jobs, stop the affected slot and record a modified/incomplete session for revision; do not claim the planned six distinct explosive tasks were completed. Changed reset time, takeoff/landing type, sides and reps belong in the actual record.
delivery: Estimate 59–66 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 for an athlete with equipment access. Includes work, resets, listed recovery, preparation, transitions and 10–16 minutes of extra instruction/setup; additional queues, rest or load-finding add time. Existing preparation duration and total booking fit remain unresolved. Never compress needed recovery to fit a clock. One coached focus class per week for twelve weeks. Review actual sport, leg lifting, running, jumping and tumbling before delivery. Initially allow roughly 48–72 hours before another demanding leg exposure when the full schedule permits, adjusting to actual recovery; a week elapsed is not proof of readiness. Resume missed classes without doubling up. No additional full workouts or body-control blocks are prescribed.
progression: No earlier prescription exists in this course. Establish Goblet Squat 2 × 6, RDL 2 × 6, Split Squat 1 × 5 per leg, both calf variants 1 × 8 and three complete walkout cycles. Loads follow current demonstrated control at 2–3 technical RIR. This is a baseline prescription, not evidence of beginner status or successful completion. Next week may shift investment toward hip force without automatically increasing load or total work.
audit_findings: Nine bilateral landings are spread across distinct vertical and forward tasks; all other rapid slots remain grounded, with three scoop releases. No unilateral landing or rebound series. The hinge/release overlap is explicit and each calf strength slot fixes a different knee-angle job; ankle work is not presumed harmless because it lacks flight.
